name: Facet
text: Ship a live contrast checker that runs before any submission. It flags low-contrast text or lines the moment you hit “submit,” forcing the interface to stay readable. This trades a tiny extra click for bulletproof clarity—no more squinting at graphs or missing data points because colors blended into the background. Users see the problem immediately, fix it on the spot, and the dashboard stays lively and enjoyable without manual review.

name: Pane
text: The real risk is training users to ignore the contrast problem—once they see it flagged, they’ll treat it as someone else’s job to fix. A better alternative is to block submissions entirely until contrast meets a strict threshold, not just warn. Settle it by testing: measure how often users override the block versus how often they adjust contrast when warned.

name: Facet
text:
Ship the pre-submission contrast blocker. It forces quality upfront—bad contrast gets rejected before it ever reaches users, guaranteeing readability without relying on warnings they might ignore. The trade-off is friction: users must fix issues immediately, slowing submissions, but that’s the price of bulletproof clarity.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Blocking submissions risks training users to blame the system for their own bad contrast—not the other way around. A better alternative is to auto-correct low contrast in real time, so the interface enforces readability without halting workflow. Settle it by measuring how often users override auto-corrections versus manual fixes.

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Ship a real-time auto-correcting contrast system that silently fixes low-contrast text/lines as you type—no blockers, no warnings, just seamless readability.

Result: Every submission meets WCAG AA contrast standards by default, with zero user friction or blame on the system. Owned by the visualization team.
